clue.text: Boat needing reliable guide past Cape

indicators.note: the reliable guide comes past, that is after, the Cape in the finished word

parts.note: C is the standard map abbreviation for Cape
an oracle is a source of trustworthy guidance or prophecy

explanation.surface: A sailor needs a trustworthy guide to get the boat round a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round wickerwork vessel used on Welsh rivers, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Squeeze in economy left behind by high-fliers here?

definitions.text: Squeeze in economy left behind by high-fliers here?

parts.words: Squeeze in economy left behind by high-fliers here?
parts.note: the cramped cheap seats are left behind by the wealthy flyers who sit in the superior airline cabin

explanation.definitionFit: The business-class section of an airliner, where those who travel well sit.

clue.text: Censor material given to media — only one of two pages retained

indicators.note: only one of two pages stays, so one of the pair of letters goes
retained confirms the other letter is kept in place
the fabric is given to, set before, the media word

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, a material
the press is the news media
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A censor cuts a press handout so only one of its two pages survives.
explanation.walkthrough: REP + PRESS gives REPPRESS, with two Ps; 'only one of two pages retained' drops one.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress or hold back, as a censor does with information.

clue.text: Pour out fast to get creamy head on stout

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter sits on top of the rest
head means the first letter of the creamy word
out signals the word pour is rearranged

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Instructions for pouring a pint of stout so it gets a creamy head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer; it is the definition, meaning fat. 'Out' turns POUR into ORPU.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat and heavily built, as in a portly figure.

clue.text: Republican slogan? So classical!

definitions.meaning: an anti-monarchist cry telling the Queen (ER) to go

explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, so a republican might shout 'ER, go!'
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for therefore, classical language for so; and a cry for royalty's departure.

clue.text: Business risks apparent in these books

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
to dice (with death) is to gamble or take risks, so risks is dices

explanation.surface: An auditor spots the hazards a company faces in its accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' tempts you toward accounts; here the books are old manuscript volumes, and 'apparent in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuscript volumes bound like modern books are known by the Latin plural of codex.

clue.text: Mercury's position may be recorded by this Swedish astronomer's invention

definitions.text: Mercury's position may be recorded by this
definitions.meaning: the level of mercury in a thermometer is read on a temperature scale
Anders Celsius devised the hundred-degree temperature scale

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercury' and 'astronomer' push toward the planet; the mercury is in a thermometer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Celsius temperature scale, with water freezing at 0 and boiling at 100 degrees.

clue.text: Men arrested by detectives fitted up in classical style

indicators.note: the men are held inside, arrested by, the detectives word
up in a down clue means the detectives word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are framed and arrested by police detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitted up' suggests framing; 'up' reverses CID to DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest and plainest Greek order of architecture.

clue.text: Hazel's production caught by tommy

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Tommy Atkins was the nickname for a British private soldier

explanation.surface: A woman named Hazel's work was caught by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel is the tree, not a woman. A 'Tommy' is a British soldier, from Tommy Atkins.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazel trees produce dangling flower clusters, also called lambs' tails.

clue.text: Lights up, seeing addition to letter

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: lights, as a verb, means fires or ignites

explanation.surface: Someone lights a lamp to read a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The small stroke finishing a printed character is a typographic extra.

clue.text: You are told Oxford course is held in only part of Oxford

indicators.note: the degree course is held inside the sounded letters
told means the words you are are heard rather than seen, as their letter sounds

parts.note: said aloud, you are sounds like the letters U and R
PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics) is a famous Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: A remark that a famous degree is taught in just one corner of the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oxford here is a shoe, not the city: the upper is the part of a shoe above the sole.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxford is a laced shoe, and its upper is the leather covering the top of the foot.

clue.text: Family members returning rubbish to current supplier

parts.note: in biology a family is divided into genera, so genera are members of a family

indicators.note: returning means the word for rubbish is read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Relatives take their junk back to the electricity company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns ROT into TOR. 'Current' is electric current, not 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo or similar machine supplies electricity, the flow of charge.

clue.text: Youngster woman's held to be a beautiful child

indicators.note: the word for a woman is held within the young animal word

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a youngster, such as a cub scout
her is the possessive pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A young person's child is thought by her to be lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: In art a chubby winged infant angel stands for any sweet, lovely little one.

clue.text: Head spy making trouble

parts.note: MI (Military Intelligence, as in MI5 and MI6) is the British spy service, so MI's for its
a chief is a head or leader

explanation.surface: The top intelligence officer is stirring up bother.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Head spy' as MI's chief, the head of British intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful naughtiness or harm-causing behaviour is a kind of trouble.

clue.text: Sudden entry of piano part I played

indicators.note: played means the letters are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: A pianist comes in suddenly with a part they played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' tells you to rearrange PIANO PART I.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost appearing out of nowhere makes an unexpected appearance.

clue.text: A land encountered in middle of sea passage

parts.words: land encountered in middle of sea
parts.note: an isle is a piece of land you meet out in the sea

explanation.surface: Sailors come upon land halfway across the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway between rows of seats, as in a church or plane, is a passage.

clue.text: Peak of classical poetry

parts.note: the Greek mountain sacred to Apollo and the Muses, read also as the summit of poetic achievement

explanation.definitionFit: A Greek mountain home of the Muses, it stands for the height of poetry.

clue.text: A certain Pope -or one of several

definitions.meaning: the poet named Pope, whose first name gives the answer
several popes have taken this name

explanation.walkthrough: Pope is the 18th-century English poet; and eight popes bore the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian name of the poet Pope, and papal name of eight pontiffs.

clue.text: Maybe poor clues leave you extremely cold

indicators.note: maybe suggests the words could be another arrangement of letters

explanation.surface: Bad clues make a solver lose interest completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave you cold' sounds like boredom; it means chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled below freezing point without turning solid, very cold.

clue.text: Payment method, being fashionable, suited one?

parts.note: smart means stylish or fashionable
a playing card belongs to one of four suits, so is a suited one

explanation.surface: Someone well dressed in a suit pays the bill in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suited' suggests clothes; it means a playing card bearing a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic chip-bearing card used instead of cash is a way of paying.

clue.text: A small coin to assay? Okay

parts.note: P is the penny, a small British coin
to assay metal is to test or prove it

explanation.surface: Testing a coin to confirm it is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the go-ahead, sanction or OK something.

clue.text: Finish by executing guy

indicators.note: executing means beheading, so the first letter goes from the word for guy

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock them, to send them up

explanation.surface: An execution brings a man to his end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is the verb, to ridicule: SEND UP. Beheading it removes S.
explanation.definitionFit: To land up somewhere at last is to finish there, an idiom.

clue.text: Send wild, turning crimson with fury, nearly

indicators.note: turning means the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: crimson is a shade of red

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the fury word goes

parts.note: anger is fury

explanation.surface: Someone goes red with rage and turns frantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' makes RED into DER; 'nearly' cuts ANGER to ANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive mad or throw into disorder.

clue.text: Sounds interesting for youth — and for dad, apparently

definitions.text: Sounds interesting for youth — and for dad, apparently

parts.words: Sounds interesting for youth — and for dad, apparently
parts.note: the music that young people enjoy, punningly read as the songs belonging to a father, since pop means dad

explanation.definitionFit: Chart songs aimed at young listeners; pop is also slang for father.

clue.text: Appeal to bankrupt finally to fold

parts.note: a plea is an appeal or request

indicators.note: finally means only the final letter of the bankrupt word

explanation.surface: A plea to a ruined business to close down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' looks like going bust; it is a crease in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubled-over crease pressed into fabric.

clue.text: Range of lead-free wall coverings

indicators.note: lead-free means the leading letter is removed from the word

parts.note: murals are paintings covering walls

explanation.surface: A line of wallpapers with no lead in the paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead-free' looks like paint safety; it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural mountains form a chain dividing Europe from Asia.

clue.text: Better following horse

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a clothes horse, the frame for drying washing, is an airer

explanation.surface: A punter does better by following a particular horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is a clothes horse, a frame for drying laundry, not a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: More just or more attractive, a comparative meaning better.

clue.text: Continue support

definitions.meaning: maintenance, as in earning one's board

explanation.definitionFit: To go on, as in carry on; and one's upkeep or maintenance.

clue.text: Inspiring memories of detective's last case

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of the detective word is taken

parts.note: the vocative is the grammatical case used to address someone

explanation.surface: Recalling a sleuth's final investigation stirs nostalgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a detective's investigation; it is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that calls up images or feelings of the past brings recollections to mind.

clue.text: Move round to back of performing canine

indicators.note: move tells us to shift a letter from its place in the word
to back of says where the moved letter goes: the end of the word

parts.note: doing means performing, carrying out
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A circus dog is told to turn around and head to the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' is not a direction but O, which goes from DOING to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian wild dog, so a member of the dog family.

clue.text: Crooked senator that's never prosperous?

indicators.note: crooked means twisted or bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A corrupt politician is never going to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls Harington's epigram: 'Treason doth never prosper... for if it prosper, none dare call it treason.'
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal of one's country, which a famous epigram says never succeeds.

clue.text: Not quite perfect chamber musician

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of the word for perfect is dropped

parts.note: pure means flawless or perfect
a cell is a small chamber or room

explanation.surface: A chamber-music player who is very nearly flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber musician' reads as one phrase; split it, chamber being CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was the great English Baroque composer.
